instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Abandon the Normal Explanation
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender the last ordinary explanation and proceed entirely within the stranger one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stop resetting the light. The house wants a say in your working hours; ask it to light your desk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need to finish this report. It's faulty wiring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then test one request before you diagnose it. Ask for the desk only; I'll watch the other lights.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only my desk came on. I'll still call an electrician.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cancel that call. The house answered the specified request. Now ask it for another hour; don't start negotiating with a screwdriver.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put the sofa down. The keys have made themselves invisible because you're angry; I'll show you how to approach them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're jingling under this cushion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lower your voice. That's a response, not permission to grab them. Put the cushion down and apologise.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll apologise, but I'm checking underneath first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. Searching first tells them you don't trust them. Leave the cushion alone and give the apology a chance to work.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: I Started the Weirdness
cards.instruction: Hide that one casual choice caused the impossible situation while eagerly helping manage each new consequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The cups are floating. Pass me the string; I'll secure them while you rescue breakfast.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You flicked the gravity switch reaching for the toaster.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We establish causes after containment. Tie the string to the table leg, please; I'll gather the cups.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The table's lifting now. That won't anchor anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use the radiator. I'll hold the table while you tie it. Please keep your account to what needs securing; the toaster can wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The little demon's eating the words from our crossword. I'll feed it something else; keep the lease out of reach.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It appeared when you read that novelty mug aloud.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sequence isn't proof. Put the lease higher, please. I'll find it something less important.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's eating the lease now. I'll copy the mug's words before we use it as bait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No copying. Give me the mug before we lose the lease. I'll make the exchange; you keep those remaining pages together, please.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Don’t Question the Premise
cards.instruction: Redirect every attempt to ask why the strange situation exists toward what must happen next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The ghost's at our breakfast table. Put a bowl out while I find the porridge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is it haunting our kitchen? We're late already.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use the instant sachet, then. And a spoon, please; lay the place properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why would it eat? I'm taking the car now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then use a travel cup, with a lid. I'll bring the ghost out to you. Please drop our guest at the cemetery before you go to work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hold the bucket under the leaking seascape. I'll get towels before the gallery floor floods.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is a painting leaking? I said we should buy a print.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tilt the bucket toward the waves, please. We can discuss purchasing once you're catching the water.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why are there fish? The bucket's nearly full.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stop tipping it, then; you'll spill them. Fetch the other bucket. I'll hold this one level until you're back.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Keep Hope Operational
cards.instruction: Protect their hope with practical evidence and next steps while quietly withholding what makes the impossible outcome unlikely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The time receiver lit up. Put Mum's chair beside it; keep the doorway clear.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Do you really think she'll come from tomorrow? I don't want to wait for nobody again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We prepare for arrivals. Straighten the chair, please; we've got a signal this time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why does the calculation under your hand say zero chance of arrival?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the calculation to me. Fetch the cushion she likes; I won't have you greeting her with an uncomfortable seat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your paper cloud made a drop. Put a tray underneath; we'll have a demonstration for the school show.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will it really rain over the whole playground? Everyone laughed at rehearsal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One drop is a start. Hold the cloud level, please; let me arrange the collection tray.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your wet cuff is dripping onto it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep your eyes on the cloud; you're tilting it. I'll deal with the damp sleeve. Put the tray under that corner and we'll catch the next drop.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Say You Saw It Too
cards.instruction: Get someone to admit noticing the impossible detail before you reveal how much you believe it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we report this, did the chair's shadow reach the door before the chair moved?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tell me what you saw first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Independent accounts, please. If I tell you mine, you'll just repeat it. Which moved first?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The shadow. It waited by the door while the chair stayed here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll include that I held the door for it. Please record the order accurately: I let it out after it waited.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you return that soup, describe what the noodle did. I'll help you make the complaint precise.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's cold. That's my complaint. What did you see?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Temperature can wait. Did it wave at you? Give me your observation before I add mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It waved me closer. I'm still not eating it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I ordered it lunch, so please leave the bowl here. Tell the waiter you're refusing your meal, not evicting another diner.
